mutant.description: NOT a planted byte mutation, and the reason is recorded rather than glossed: every limb of this act's claim lives on the live S3/host plane or in an append-only shared file, so planting would have meant mutating served state or creating a transient false OPEN that a peer's deploy_ledger.py check --red sweep could escalate on. The DEPLOY genre exists for this case but is NOT claimed: the governing order carries <risk>WORLD</risk> and no <proof_genre>DEPLOY</proof_genre> line at HEAD, and DEPLOY is never self-declared. The controls used instead are STATE-BASED. (1) THE BASE/CUT DISCRIMINATION PAIR, run in both directions across the apply. (2) THE AC1 TWO-STATE CONTROL. (3) A NAME-DROP CONTROL on the tool census. (4) A BUMP-ONE CONTROL on the A1 link counts, plus a MECHANISM control for how those counts are computed off-host. (5) THE HALT GATE's refusal/admission pair, built on a limb the gate actually reads. (6) THE CUT-METHOD CONTROL against the trunk. (7) The issuer's own pre-cut dry run, which recorded all three criteria FAILING at the base.

Graded as BUILD, which is why the state-based controls above were recorded rather than a redeploy exemption asserted. The named rollback is on the rollback artifact's own row and in the ledger entry.

declared_exclusions.item: Rolling back v1 in order to ship v2 as a single release.
declared_exclusions.reason: Never considered necessary and explicitly excluded by A6: v1 is correct on every limb it was graded on and is v2's rollback key. The order shipped in two acts because A4 weighed the 10:00Z slot against a naming-gate fix that had no owner yet (row Z-W34-S7, with 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z) and chose to deliver FWD-20's depth and durable key immediately with FWD-21 short at 1 of 7 research tables; A6 then re-opened for a catalog-only v2 once MX-c-9 A3+A4 drained with research 7 of 7. Both acts are recorded here, both ran under their own signed never-widen pair and their own NEVER-2 ledger, and neither was rolled back.

declared_exclusions.item: MX-c-9 A3's six hyphenated research rows, and therefore 6 of the 7 research tables.
declared_exclusions.reason: ABSENT BY ORDER, not by defect, and the order says so in A4 @8607bd9a82: .tools/naming-gate.py does not read legacy_addresses.json, so the six rows' emitted prefix values grade NEW OUT-OF-PATTERN and cannot be committed. The gate is LGIC_ENFORCE's and the ask is with 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z (the issuer's row Z-W34-S7). A3 had held PHASE A for that drain precisely so the release would not ship a six-row-short catalog; A4 then weighed the 10:00Z slot against a gate fix with no owner yet and ruled the three committed blobs ship now, with the six rows riding the next gateway release. So this release delivers FWD-20 depth and the durable index key, and FWD-21 at 24 of 24 top-level prefixes with 1 of 7 research tables. r12.AC2 and r12.AC3 do not count research tables and therefore stand as written -- which is the reason the partial delivery is gradeable at all. Also per A4: had the gate fix landed and MX-c-9 A3 committed BEFORE the never-widen pair was signed, PHASE A would have been re-cut once on the new catalog blob; it did not, so the cut stands. This row is NOT listed under `surprises` because it is the issuer's open item about content this order was ORDERED to omit, not a surprise this act surfaced, and listing it would gate a flip that A4 already dispositioned.

declared_exclusions.item: Any merge of box/sitez into the deploy tree.
declared_exclusions.reason: Forbidden by order item 1 and by the MX-r-11 v2 lesson, and the cost was measured rather than assumed: 32 gateway paths differ between the cut and the trunk, including deploy-to-ec2.sh itself, so a merge would have shipped 32 files where 3 were signed for and would have voided both halves on 'a deploy script other than the base's'. The cut is a single-blob-set overlay on the live ref's tree through a temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE -- which also keeps anything else in the worktree (including the wrapper's later manifest edit) out of the shipped tree by construction rather than by care.

declared_exclusions.item: Typing any of the three shipped blob ids from the issuer's abbreviations.
declared_exclusions.reason: Declared because the first attempt did exactly that and was refused. Expanding `f15b348263` into a plausible 40-character hash produced an id no object has, and git rejected the index with 'invalid object' -- the correct outcome, and a reminder that an abbreviation is a CHECK, not an input. Every shipped blob was then resolved with `git rev-parse 435958cd7c:<path>` and the issuer's abbreviation asserted as a prefix of what resolved; all three matched, and all three are equal at box/sitez HEAD, so nothing drifted between the drain and the cut.

declared_exclusions.item: A third apply to correct the deploy tree's uncommitted EC2_MANIFEST.json.
declared_exclusions.reason: Deliberately left uncommitted in C:/tmp/mx-dep-r12, as on MX-r-11. safe-ec2-deploy.sh's helper writes previous_deployed_commit from the release tree's own chain vintage and keeps the prior release_note; its commit fails closed there (the commit-gate import closure is outside the cone), and had it succeeded it would have moved the detached deploy tree's HEAD off the cut, breaking the label-names-the-bytes property row Z-S92 exists to protect. The file sits outside $SRC so it cannot enter the tar. The authoritative plane-2 write was made by hand with a precondition and a changed-field assertion.
